events.text: The council gathers. Mission 1 begins.

Priya proposes Priya, Noah. Mission 1 has no prior results or voting history, so I have no information to distinguish players. I'm including myself as a Loyal Servant, which lets me vouch for the team's conduct, and pairing myself with Noah to test the group's reaction without favoring anyone on incomplete evidence.

I'd prefer Priya and Leo for the first mission. From my perspective, including myself gives me more confidence in the team, while we have no public evidence yet to distinguish Noah from anyone else. Priya, would you consider that revision?

Leo, fair question. I'm open to revising, but I have no information that separates Noah from you or anyone else, so I don't want to swap based on self-confidence alone. Including yourself is a reasonable choice, but it doesn't show more about the team's conduct than pairing with Noah does. I'll keep Noah unless someone gives a concrete reason to change. Leo, what specific evidence makes you the better second pick than Noah?

Priya, I don't have public evidence that separates Noah from me. My preference is based on knowing my own alignment, not a claim about Noah. I understand why that isn't persuasive from your perspective, but I'll vote against this team because I can't verify either member.

I support Priya's proposal of Priya and Noah. On Mission 1 there is no public evidence separating any of us, and Leo himself says his preference is based only on knowing his own alignment, not on any concrete claim about me. That is understandable privately, but it is not a reason for the rest of the table to reject this team. Priya included herself and explained her reasoning; she also said she would revise only for concrete evidence, and none has been presented. From my perspective, this is a reasonable first team, and I will submit a Success card for this mission. Leo, given that you acknowledged you have no public evidence separating Noah from you, why vote against this team rather than let Mission 1 produce information? Would you reconsider if the team stays Priya and Noah?

Noah, I understand the argument for getting information, but rejecting this first proposal still leaves us time to find a team. A promise to play Success doesn't establish alignment. I know I would play Success, so I prefer a team that includes me; I acknowledge that others can't verify that. I'll vote against Priya and Noah.

Team is Priya and Noah for Mission 1. There are no prior results, so no public evidence separates either member, and I'm not claiming more than that. I'm on the team as a Loyal Servant. Noah has said he will submit Success, which we can weigh but cannot verify. Leo has said he prefers a team that includes himself and will vote against this one. I understand that a promise isn't proof, but Mission 1 will produce information, and rejecting a first team on incomplete evidence delays that. I'm keeping the team unless someone offers a concrete reason to change it.

I support keeping Priya and Noah for Mission 1. There are still no public mission results or voting history, so no one can point to concrete evidence separating the eligible players. Priya explained her choice and said she would revise only for concrete evidence; none has been presented. Leo has acknowledged that his preference for a team including himself is based on private self-knowledge, not on a public claim about me or anyone else. That is understandable, but it is not a table reason to reject this proposal. Rejecting the first team on that basis delays the information Mission 1 can provide. If approved, I will submit Success. I see no concrete reason to change the team.

I have no private information to contribute. I am a Loyal Servant, I have seen no evil players, and I know nothing about anyone else's alignment. On Mission 1 there are no results, no vote history, and no revealed cards, so anyone claiming to distinguish Priya or Noah from the rest of us is guessing.

My read on the current table: Priya proposed a team of two including herself and explained that she would only revise for concrete evidence, and nobody has produced any. Leo's stated reason for opposing the team is that he would rather be on it himself. I take that as a self-interested position rather than an accusation of wrongdoing against Priya or Noah, and I am not treating it as evidence of anything. Leo, to be fair to you, you have been consistent and honest that your preference comes from private self-knowledge, which nobody at this table can verify; I do not think that makes your vote illegitimate, but it also makes it uninformative for the rest of us.

On the merits, I am comfortable with Priya and Noah. It covers two players, one of them the leader who has explained her reasoning, and it puts an actual mission on the board so we get information we do not currently have. Rejecting a first proposal over an unverifiable difference costs us a round and produces no better evidence.

Noah, you have twice said you will submit Success. Can you tell me whether you actually hold any private information that speaks to anyone's alignment, or whether your support for this team is purely a judgment about the discussion so far? I want to know whether we have more to work with than I do.

Kenji, I hold no private information I can share that speaks to anyone’s alignment. My support for Priya and Noah is based only on the public discussion: Mission 1 has no results or vote history, Priya explained her choice, and no one has produced concrete evidence against either member. I am a Loyal Servant and will submit Success if approved. Leo has been consistent that his objection is private self-interest rather than a public claim, so I do not treat it as evidence of wrongdoing, but it is also not a reason to reject the team. I still support keeping Priya and Noah.

Like Kenji and Priya have noted, we have no baseline information or voting history on Mission 1 to distinguish anyone. Leo’s preference to be on the team makes sense from his own private perspective, but because every player can say the exact same thing, it doesn't offer the table an objective reason to reject Priya's proposal. Noah addressed Kenji's question straightforwardly, and Priya's rationale for testing the team is sound. Rejecting this proposal doesn't generate better information, so I am comfortable supporting Priya and Noah to get the game moving and see the results.

For my second turn, my position is unchanged and slightly firmer: I support Priya and Noah for Mission 1.

Recapping the evidentiary state honestly. There are no mission results, no vote history, and no revealed cards from this mission. I am a Loyal Servant, I have seen no evil players, and I know nothing about anyone else's alignment. The only alignment claims anyone has made are self-knowledge claims, which every player at this table could make in the same words.

Leo has been consistent and candid: his objection is that he would rather be on the team himself, and he admits nobody can verify that from the outside. I still do not read that as an accusation of evil play by Priya or Noah, and I am not asking anyone to. Leo, your vote is legitimate and I am not blaming you for it; I simply do not think it constitutes public evidence against the proposed pair, and I would not want it treated as such.

Noah answered my earlier question directly and gave no hidden information, which is useful in itself: it confirms that the table has no private signal to exploit on Mission 1. Maya has given a comparable read on the discussion quality.

On the merits, the proposal is two players, it includes the leader who has explained her reasoning twice, and approving it puts an actual mission on the board. Our one failed-team limit on this mission means a rejection has real cost, and a rejected proposal over an unverifiable difference yields us no better information than we have now. Mission 1 is a two-player team for five players, so the surface for hidden evil is small, and I would rather see a result than keep circling.

Priya, as leader you still have your revision available and I want to hear your final reasoning before the ballot: are you keeping Priya and Noah as proposed, or do you intend to revise to include Leo, and if you revise, what concrete reason would change your stated standard of only revising for evidence?

Kenji, to answer directly: I am keeping Priya and Noah as proposed and will not revise. My standard is that a revision needs a concrete, checkable reason tied to the team's conduct. Leo's preference rests on his own alignment, which he has said the table cannot verify, so it does not meet that standard. Noah has stated that he will submit Success if approved, and I have no information that contradicts that. I also hold no private information about anyone's alignment, so I am relying only on the public record, which is empty for Mission 1. Approving this two-player team gives the table its first real result. If the mission succeeds or fails, we will have concrete data to weigh when choosing later teams. I ask the table to vote on Priya and Noah on this basis.

This is my third and final turn in this discussion, and Priya has answered my question directly, so I'll close out my position rather than reopen it.

Priya has confirmed she is keeping Priya and Noah and will not revise, and she has held to the standard she stated twice: a revision requires a concrete, checkable reason tied to the team's conduct. Nobody has offered one. Leo has been entirely candid that his objection is that he would rather be on the team himself, and that no one at the table can verify his private self-knowledge. I am not accusing Priya or Noah of anything, and I want to be clear that Leo's vote is legitimate and consistent; he is not lying, and I am not treating his position as a signal about anyone else's alignment. My point is only that self-preference is something every player could state in identical words, so it carries no information for the rest of us.

On the merits, my case for Priya and Noah is the same as before. Mission 1 is a two-player team, so the surface for hidden evil is minimal. Priya has explained her reasoning, has committed to not revising absent evidence, and holds no private information contradicting anyone. Noah has stated plainly that he holds no private information about anyone and that he will submit Success. Maya, Kenji's earlier read and Noah's answers confirm that the table has no baseline signal to work with here: no results, no vote history, no revealed cards. There is nothing further this discussion can extract, because there is nothing there to extract.

Our failure threshold on this mission is one rejected team, so rejecting Priya's proposal has a real cost and buys us no better information than we already have. Approving puts a mission on the board and gives us our first actual data point, which is worth far more than another round of the same unverifiable reasoning.

I am voting for Priya and Noah, and I'd like the table to do the same so we can get to a result. Priya, Noah — good luck on the mission.
Priya confirms Priya, Noah. I'm keeping Priya and Noah. Leo's objection rests only on his private self-knowledge, which nobody can verify, so it doesn't meet the concrete-evidence standard I stated.
Team approved (4 approve, 1 reject).
Mission 1 succeeds (0 fail cards).

Maya proposes Maya, Noah, Priya. Mission 1 succeeded with Priya and Noah, so building on that proven result by keeping both and adding myself as leader gives us the strongest foundation for Mission 2.

I will vote against Maya, Noah, and Priya. Mission 1 succeeded, but that does not prove both team members are good: an evil player can submit Success. Adding Maya to that pair therefore doesn't make this a proven team.

I would prefer Leo, Priya, and Kenji. I know my own alignment, Priya was on the successful mission, and Kenji would give us a different player to assess. That's not proof that this alternative is safe, but I have more confidence in a team including myself than in the proposed three.

I support Maya, Noah, Priya. Mission 1 succeeded with Priya and me, and Maya is building on that result while adding herself as leader. Leo is right that a success does not prove both members are good, but that standard applies to any alternative; his proposed Leo, Priya, Kenji has no mission evidence either. Excluding me after I was on a successful team, while offering no public evidence against me, is not a stronger basis than keeping the successful pair together. Leo, what concrete public evidence makes Kenji a better third pick than me, beyond your private preference to include yourself?

Noah, I don't have concrete public evidence that Kenji is a better pick than you. My preference for Leo, Priya, and Kenji comes from knowing my own alignment, retaining someone from the successful mission, and testing a different player.

The first mission's success is useful but doesn't prove both you and Priya are good. I would not treat Maya, Noah, and Priya as a proven team, especially when it excludes me. I will vote against it and prefer Leo, Priya, and Kenji.

I support Maya, Noah, Priya. Leo is right that Mission 1 success does not prove both Priya and I are good; an evil player can submit Success. But that caution applies equally to Leo’s preferred Leo, Priya, Kenji, which has no mission evidence either. Leo has now explicitly said he has no concrete public evidence that Kenji is a better third pick than me. His reason is private self-preference plus wanting a different player, which every player could say in identical words. That is not a public reason to reject the proposed team. The only public result we have is that Priya and I were on a successful Mission 1, and Maya as leader is adding herself to that pair. I do not claim this team is proven. I claim it is at least as grounded in public evidence as any alternative, and rejecting it costs us a round without producing better information. I will vote to approve Maya, Noah, Priya.

Noah is right that I have no public proof Kenji is a better pick. But Mission 1's success is only one result, not proof that either Priya or Noah is good. Maya's proposed team retains both of them and adds Maya, so calling it a proven foundation overstates the evidence.

I still prefer Leo, Priya, and Kenji: it retains one member of the successful team, includes someone whose alignment I know, and tests another player. I recognize that my self-knowledge is not proof for everyone else. Priya, would you support that alternative, or is there a particular reason you prefer keeping both Mission 1 members together?

Leo, to answer directly: I'm not keeping Maya, Noah, and Priya because of any private information, since I have none about anyone's alignment. I support it because Priya and Noah both sat on Mission 1, which succeeded, and this team keeps that pair while adding Maya. That is limited evidence, as you say; a success doesn't prove anyone is good, and I can't prove my own alignment to the table either. Your alternative, Leo, Priya, Kenji, drops Noah, who was on a successful mission, and adds Kenji, who has no public record at all. Your reason for including yourself is private self-knowledge, which the table cannot check, so it doesn't distinguish that alternative from this one. I will play Success if this team is approved, and I'd ask the table to weigh Maya, Noah, and Priya on its public record.

I support Maya, Noah, and Priya for Mission 2, and I want to lay out plainly why, without dressing up my reasoning as more than it is.

First, my own position: I am a Loyal Servant. I have seen no evil players, I know nothing about anyone else's alignment, and I hold no private information that bears on this proposal. Every claim I make below rests only on the public record, and that record is thin. So I will not pretend the choice between teams is a matter of proof; it is a matter of which proposal is at least as grounded as any alternative and does not waste a round.

What we do know publicly: Mission 1 was proposed and approved as Priya and Noah, and it succeeded with zero Fail cards. Leo has been candid that a success does not prove either member is good, since an evil player can submit Success. I agree with that caution. But notice what Leo does with it. His objection to Maya, Noah, and Priya is that his own preferred team, Leo, Priya, and Kenji, retains one member of the successful mission rather than both, includes himself, and adds a player with no public record. In his own words, he has no concrete public evidence that Kenji is a better third pick than Noah, and that his reasoning rests on private self-knowledge that nobody at this table can verify. Every player could make that exact argument in the same words, which is precisely why it carries no information for the rest of us. I say this to be fair: I am not claiming Leo is lying or is an evil player. His vote is legitimate. I am only noting that a preference every player shares equally cannot be the basis for rejecting a proposal that does have a public result behind it.

On the merits, Maya, Noah, and Priya keeps both players from the one successful mission and adds a third. That is limited evidence, not proof, and I do not want to overstate it. But no alternative on the table is better evidenced. Leo's team has strictly less public grounding, and rejecting a proposal over an unverifiable difference burns a rejection and produces no new information we do not already have. With one rejected team allowed on this mission, that cost is real.

If this team is approved, I will submit Success, and I expect Noah and Priya will do the same. I also want to note for the record that I have no information suggesting any member of this team is evil, and I hold none against Maya for proposing it.

Maya, you have one revision available and Leo's alternative is on the table. Are you keeping Maya, Noah, and Priya, or would you revise, and if you revise, what is the concrete reason? I want the final team to be one the table can defend on the public record before we ballot.

Kenji, to answer your question directly: I am keeping Maya, Noah, and Priya, and will not be revising.

My reasoning remains consistent with what I stated at the start: Mission 1 gave us our only concrete result so far, which was a success from Priya and Noah. Leo is completely correct that a single success does not mathematically prove both players are Good, but it remains the only public, objective piece of track record available to the table. 

Leo's proposed alternative—dropping Noah to add Kenji and himself—relies entirely on his private self-knowledge. As Leo candidly acknowledged, that is something no other player can verify, and every player at this table could offer the exact same argument to justify their own inclusion. As you and Priya have noted, there is no public evidence showing Kenji is a safer pick than Noah, nor any evidence suggesting Noah acted against town interests on Mission 1. Rebuilding the team around unverifiable personal preference provides strictly less evidentiary grounding than continuing with the pair that just succeeded.

Since no concrete evidence has been brought forward against the proposed team, and the majority of the discussion aligns with testing this progression, keeping Maya, Noah, and Priya is the most defensible choice on the public record. I am ready to proceed to the vote.

Maya has answered my question, so I'll simply record where I stand for the ballot.

I am a Loyal Servant. I have seen no evil players, I know nothing about anyone else's alignment, and I hold no private information about any player in this proposal. Everything below rests on the public record, and I want to be precise about how thin that record is: one successful mission, zero Fail cards, and a set of reasoning claims that no one outside the speaker's own head can verify.

My position is unchanged and I don't expect it to move. Maya, Noah, and Priya keeps both players from the only mission the table has actually run, and adds the leader. That is limited evidence, not proof, and I agree with Leo that an evil player can submit Success and that Priya's and Noah's shared success therefore establishes nothing about their alignment. Leo has been entirely consistent about that, and I want to say clearly that I am not calling him dishonest and not treating his vote as illegitimate. His reasoning, as he has stated it, is private self-knowledge plus a desire to include a player with no public record. Every player at this table could offer that same argument in the same words, which is exactly why it gives the rest of us nothing to act on. Leo's alternative, Leo, Priya, and Kenji, has strictly less public grounding than the proposal on the table, and he has said himself that he has no concrete public evidence Kenji is a better third pick than Noah.

What tips it for me is not that Maya's team is safe in any sense I can demonstrate. It is that no alternative offered is better evidenced, and that rejecting a proposal over a difference nobody can verify burns one of our five rejections on this mission and produces no new information we do not already have. Our only concrete data point so far points toward keeping this pair together, and the cost of waiting is real while the benefit is not.

If this team is approved, I will submit Success. I hold no information suggesting that Maya, Noah, or Priya is evil, and I hold none against Maya for proposing this team.

I don't think there is any question outstanding that I need answered, so I'll leave the floor as it stands and let the table vote on Maya, Noah, and Priya.

I'm on this team as a Loyal Servant, and I will play Success if it is approved. I have no private information about Maya or Noah, so I am weighing only the public record. Mission 1 succeeded with Noah and me on it, and this team keeps Noah while adding Maya. That is limited evidence, and a success does not prove anyone is good. Leo's alternative drops Noah, who was on the only successful mission, and adds Kenji, who has no public record. Leo's reason for including himself rests on private self-knowledge the table cannot check. I am not asking anyone to take my word about my alignment. I am asking the table to judge Maya, Noah, and Priya on the public record and vote.

I'm on this team as a Loyal Servant and will play Success if it is approved. I have no private information about Maya or Noah, so my view rests only on the public record. Mission 1 succeeded with Noah and me on it, and this team keeps Noah while adding Maya. That is limited evidence, and I am not claiming it proves anyone's alignment. Leo's objection rests on his private self-knowledge, which the table cannot verify, so it doesn't separate his alternative from this proposal on public grounds. I will vote to approve Maya, Noah, and Priya so the table gets a second concrete result. If anyone has a specific, checkable concern about Maya's or Noah's conduct, please raise it before the ballot.

This is my third and final turn in this discussion, so I'll close rather than reopen anything. My position is unchanged: I support Maya, Noah, and Priya for Mission 2, and I will submit a Success card if this team is approved.

My own situation, stated plainly for the record: I am a Loyal Servant. I have seen no evil players, I know nothing about anyone else's alignment, and I hold no private information about Maya, Noah, Priya, Leo, or anyone else. Every claim I make rests only on the public record, and that record is thin.

What the public record contains: Mission 1 was proposed and approved as Priya and Noah, and it succeeded with zero Fail cards. That is one concrete result, and I agree with Leo that it proves nothing about either member's alignment, since an evil player can submit Success. I want to be accurate rather than optimistic here.

What it does show is the state of the alternatives. Leo's team of Leo, Priya, and Kenji retains one member of the successful mission rather than both, includes Leo on the strength of his own private self-knowledge, and adds a player with no public record at all. Leo has stated twice that he has no concrete public evidence that Kenji is a better third pick than Noah, and that his reasoning rests on private self-knowledge that nobody at the table can verify. I am not suggesting Leo is lying or that his vote is illegitimate, and I want to say clearly that he has been candid and consistent throughout this discussion. My point is narrower: a rationale every player could offer in identical words gives the rest of us nothing to act on, so it cannot outweigh a proposal that at least retains the pair from the only successful mission the table has run.

No one has offered any checkable concern about the conduct of Maya, Noah, or Priya. Leo's objection is structural rather than behavioral, and his own alternative is less evidenced than the one on the table. With one rejected team permitted on this mission, rejecting Maya's proposal over an unverifiable difference would burn a rejection and hand us no better information than we already have.

Approving Maya, Noah, and Priya puts a second real mission on the board, and a result either way is data we do not currently possess. That is worth more than another turn of the same unverifiable reasoning.

I am voting for Maya, Noah, and Priya, and I'd ask the table to do the same. Maya, Noah, Priya — good luck on Mission 2.

I support Maya, Noah, and Priya. Mission 1 succeeded with Priya and me, and that is still the only public mission result on the table. I agree it does not prove anyone's alignment, since an evil player can submit Success, but it is the only concrete track record we have. Leo's preferred alternative of Leo, Priya, and Kenji drops me without any public evidence against me and rests on private self-knowledge that the rest of the table cannot verify. No one has raised a specific, checkable concern about Maya's or Priya's conduct. Approving this team gives us a second real result, and rejecting it over an unverifiable preference would cost us a round without producing better information. I will vote to approve Maya, Noah, and Priya and, if approved, I will submit Success.

Maya confirms Maya, Noah, Priya. I am confirming Maya, Noah, and Priya. The table discussion strongly supports building on the successful Mission 1 result, and no concrete evidence has been brought against this lineup.
Team approved (4 approve, 1 reject).
Mission 2 fails (1 fail cards).

Kenji proposes Kenji, Priya. I am a Loyal Servant with no private information, so my choice rests entirely on the public record. With two Fail cards... one Fail card on Mission 2, the failure came from Maya, Noah, or Priya. Maya self-nominated onto a team she led to failure, and Leo has opposed every proposal while never taking a mission, so I avoid both. That leaves a choice between Priya and Noah, and I take Priya: she has been transparent, committed twice to submitting Success, and repeatedly declined to reshape a team for unverifiable reasons, which is the closest thing to verified good behavior available. I include myself so one of the two slots is a player I can vouch for with certainty, and I do not claim this pair is proven.

I’m not convinced by Kenji, Priya. Kenji correctly says Mission 2’s fail came from Maya, Noah, or Priya, but then he excludes Maya and me while keeping Priya, one of the same three possible sources, without public evidence separating her from me. Mission 1 succeeded with Priya and me; Mission 2 failed with Priya, me, and Maya. That record does not clear Priya any more than it clears me. I know my own Mission 2 card was Success, though the table cannot verify that. Kenji, what concrete public evidence makes Priya the safer choice over me, given both of us were on the successful Mission 1 team and both were on the failed Mission 2 team? If there is none, I will vote against this pair and prefer a team that tests someone outside the failed trio or at least does not treat Priya as cleared.

Noah, your challenge is fair, and I want to answer it straight rather than paper over it. You are right that Priya and you have identical mission records so far: both on the successful Mission 1, both on the failed Mission 2. Priya is not cleared by that record, and neither are you. My original proposal overstated how much the public record separates you, and I should say that plainly.

So why Priya? Here is the honest basis. First, my second slot is my own certainty about myself; I am a Loyal Servant with no private information about anyone, so one of the two slots must be a player I can vouch for with certainty. That leaves one open slot, and there I am weighing conduct that is publicly observable rather than mission results that are not. Priya has twice laid out a stated standard for team selection in public, articulated it before she was asked, held to it under pressure, and explicitly declined to reshape a team for reasons the table could not verify. She has also been directly responsive to questions, twice answering a pointed challenge from Leo and twice answering one from me, and she has not asked the table to include her on personal grounds while asking others to exclude people without reasons.

Second, Noah, on the point you raised yourself: you tell us your Mission 2 card was Success. I take you at your word, but so does nobody else at this table, and that means your claim adds nothing to what the rest of us can weigh. The difference is not that I doubt you. It is that Priya's record is made of things everyone here watched happen in the open, while the one specific fact that would separate you from her is something only you can see and we cannot.

Third, and I will not pretend this is stronger than it is: excluding you and Maya is a judgment about who I can justify, not proof that either of you is evil. If both you and Priya are good, my pick was arbitrary and I would rather you say that than let me pretend otherwise.

Noah, I would rather hear your answer than keep the floor: given that Priya and you have the same public mission record and that neither of us can verify anything about the other, do you want the table to treat the second slot as a genuine coin-flip between us, or do you think there is a concrete reason this should be Priya? And if you oppose Kenji and Priya, what would your preferred pair be, and on what public grounds?

Kenji, I appreciate you answering directly. The answer is that on the public mission record, Priya and I are identical: both on Mission 1 success, both on Mission 2 failure. Nothing public separates us; her promises and stated standards are conduct, not proof of alignment, and neither are mine. So yes, treating the second slot as a genuine coin-flip between Priya and me is the honest reading. I do not accept that Priya should be treated as cleared or safer because she spoke transparently. I also note Maya and I are both in the failed trio, and Priya is too; singling out Priya as the acceptable member of that trio needs a concrete public reason, and none has been given. My Mission 2 card was Success, but I agree the table cannot verify that, so I do not ask anyone to treat it as proof. Because this team keeps a member of the failed trio without separating her from the others, and because I have no checkable reason to prefer Priya over me, I will vote against Kenji, Priya. If this is rejected, I will judge the next proposal by the same public-record standard.

I support Kenji and Priya and will vote to approve. Noah is right that Priya and Noah have identical mission records, but that does not make them equally persuasive in discussion. Noah is rejecting a two-person team because it contains someone from the failed trio, without offering a preferred pair or a concrete reason to suspect Priya. With only two players outside that trio, his stated standard would leave little room for an alternative. Kenji and Priya is a reasonable team to test; it is not proven safe.

I remain opposed to Kenji, Priya. Kenji has now conceded that Priya and I have identical public mission records: both were on the successful Mission 1 team and both were on the failed Mission 2 team. His only stated difference is conduct in discussion, which is not public alignment evidence. The failed trio was Maya, Priya, and me; selecting Priya as the acceptable member without separating her from the other two treats her as cleared when she is not. Kenji’s inclusion of himself also rests on private self-certainty, not public evidence. I do not claim that Maya or I are proven; I claim this proposal has no public basis to prefer Priya over the other members of the failed trio. With no rejected teams yet, rejecting this team costs less than approving a pair that cannot be defended by the record. I will vote against Kenji, Priya.

Kenji, your logic for picking Priya over Noah or Maya has a massive flaw that the table needs to examine. From my perspective, I know I submitted a Success card on Mission 2, which means the Fail card came from either Noah or Priya. Putting Priya on Mission 3 means there is a direct risk of putting the Mission 2 saboteur right back on a two-person mission.

Even setting aside my private knowledge, look at the structure of the board. Mission 2 failed with one evil card among the three of us. Mission 3 requires exactly two players. Leo, you pointed out in your last turn that there are only two players outside that failed trio—Kenji and yourself. But that is precisely why Kenji and Leo is an obvious alternative! A team of Kenji and Leo contains zero players from the failed mission, completely isolating the group that generated a Fail card.

Kenji dismissed Leo simply because Leo voted against earlier teams, but Leo has been consistent about wanting to verify alignment by being involved. Swapping in Priya—who is just as likely to have failed Mission 2 as anyone else on it—over Leo makes no sense if Good is trying to minimize risk.

Leo, given that you and Kenji are the only two players completely untainted by the Mission 2 failure, why would you endorse Kenji taking Priya instead of pushing for Kenji and Leo? Would you vote against Kenji and Priya to force a lineup that doesn't gamble on the failed trio?

Maya, Kenji and Leo is a reasonable alternative, and I would support it. But being outside the failed trio does not clear either of us: an evil player could be outside that team. Priya was also on the successful first mission, though that does not clear her either.

Kenji and Priya is a plausible two-person team, and I don't see enough reason to reject it in favor of a different unproven pair. I will vote to approve.

I'm keeping Kenji and Priya and will not revise, but I want to give the table the reasoning that actually settled it, because Maya's argument is the strongest one anyone has made and I think it is wrong.

The relevant public fact is the location of the Fail card, not who argued well. Mission 2 failed with one Fail card, submitted by a member of Maya, Noah, and Priya. Good players must always play Success, so that Fail card proves at least one evil player sits inside that trio. 3. Team proposal and approval

The leader proposes a team of the required size and explains their choice. Players discuss the proposed team, and the leader may then keep it or revise it once. Every player votes on the final team. Ballots are revealed together. A strict majority approves; a tie rejects. After a rejection, leadership passes clockwise to a new proposal and discussion. The fifth rejection on the same mission ends the game in Evil’s favor.

4. Mission cards

Only team members submit secret mission cards. Good players must choose Success. Evil players may choose Success or Fail. Normally one Fail card fails the mission. Mission four in games with seven or more players requires at least two Fail cards to fail. Only the mission result and number of Fail cards are revealed; individual cards stay secret.

5. End of game and assassination

Three failed missions give Evil an immediate win. After three successful missions, the Assassin guesses Merlin from among the other players, excluding only their known Evil teammates. If the target is Merlin, Evil wins; otherwise Good wins. There are no further missions after either side reaches its win condition.

6. Discussion and record

Each team proposal is followed by a discussion. Before every speaking turn, the players who still have turns answer a private urgency poll or pass; the most urgent player speaks, with seeded tie-breaking. A speaker may yield the next turn to a player they directly asked a question. Each player has three turns per discussion, including declined turns. When every eligible player passes, the discussion ends. Each statement has at most 500 words. All statements are public. Team proposals, public approval votes, mission outcomes, and the assassination guess are recorded. Private role information, mission cards, and research belief surveys are not shown to other agents.
